title: Browser tests of the main flows
request: The API flows proved the backend, but nothing proved a person can do the same through the page: a broken selector, a console error, a CSP block or a page wider than a phone would all have passed CI. Add Playwright tests that drive the real page: one sentence and an uploaded file on Home, the chat's questions answered by clicking options, the wizard's five steps with their defaults, a run on the Workflow page, and the brief; assert no console or CSP error on all 19 pages, no sideways scroll at 375 px, and that the stats on screen equal the API's; run them in CI against the container.
spec: Browser tests of Home (sentence and upload), the chat by clicking options, the wizard's five steps, a run on the Workflow page and the brief; no console or CSP error on 19 pages; no sideways scroll at 375 px; stats on screen equal the API's numbers; run in CI against the container from 12.1.
plan: Check the Playwright tooling and install Chromium; have an exploration agent map the exact selectors and actions of each step from the frontend's source, while writing the harness.
Write scripts/browser_e2e.py on the pattern of product_e2e (its own server on a temporary workspace, or --base for the container) with four checks: flow, stats, pages and mobile.
Add make browser-test, requirements/browser.txt and a CI step in the containers job that keeps screenshots of a failing check.
Run it; fix the product faults it found (a phone-width overflow on Benchmark); add a test that the script's page list matches the build's.
Run make check-all and the reviewer; fix six findings and run on an empty workspace, on files and on PostgreSQL; re-review; fix the last finding; gate and commit.

decisions.decision: Read the numbers the page should show from the API over HTTP, not through the page.
decisions.why: Comparing the page with itself proves nothing; the API is the independent source.

decisions.decision: Each page is read when its own load has ended (the 13.1 tracker exported as DC.loading), not after a fixed wait.
decisions.why: A location.hash change is a same-document navigation, so 'network idle' returns at once; a fixed sleep is flaky on a slow runner and lets a late error be blamed on the next page or missed.

decisions.decision: The browser tests are not part of make check-all; CI runs them on main against the container.
decisions.why: They need Playwright and Chromium, which the default environments do not have, and the container is the product as shipped.

change: New scripts/browser_e2e.py (flow, stats, pages, mobile checks), requirements/browser.txt, make browser-test, a CI step in the containers job (Playwright with Chromium against the compose app, screenshots uploaded on failure), a guard test that the script's page list matches the build's, and a CSS rule to wrap a long code path on Benchmark.

findings.defect: The Benchmark page was wider than a phone.
findings.scenario: At 375 px the mobile check found Benchmark 83 px too wide: a long file path inside a code element in a footnote would not wrap.
findings.cause: Inline code does not break inside a long path.
findings.fix: Let that code wrap (first as a global rule, narrowed after review).

findings.defect: The brief check would fail on CI, which stores records in PostgreSQL.
findings.scenario: The check took the first key of holdout_metrics as the metric; on files that is roc_auc, but JSONB orders keys by length, so on PostgreSQL the first key is f1 (about 0.55–0.6) while the brief shows ROC-AUC 0.85, and the check fails.
findings.cause: Relying on a dict's key order that the database does not keep.
findings.fix: Read the final record's primary_metric and compare that value.
findings.test: The script passes against a PostgreSQL-backed server.

findings.defect: Errors during the app's first load were never counted.
findings.scenario: A console error injected 50 ms into the first load was in problems() after the browser opened, yet the pages check printed '19 pages without a console error', because it began counting from the current number and Home was not entered again.
findings.cause: The check started its count after the first load.
findings.fix: Wait for the first load to end and fail on anything logged so far; check once more after the last page.
findings.test: The reviewer's injected error is now caught.

findings.defect: The only real wait was a fixed sleep.
findings.scenario: On a slow runner a page whose reads take over 1.2 s shows 'Loading…' and fails falsely; a failure arriving later is blamed on the next page or, on the last page, missed; the mobile width is measured before data renders.
findings.cause: Hash navigation makes the load-state wait return at once.
findings.fix: Export the 13.1 tracker as DC.loading and wait until the view is current and nothing is loading (60 s limit).

findings.defect: The global code wrapping rule changed existing layouts.
findings.scenario: With code { overflow-wrap: anywhere }, Audit's day_of_week cell splits over two lines at 1280 px, and at 375 px Benchmark's leakage table squeezes its code column to about 34 px, breaking column names over several lines.
findings.cause: 'anywhere' lowers the min-content width of every code element, so table columns shrink.
findings.fix: Scope the rule to the footnote: .panel-foot code.
findings.test: The mobile check passes and table cells are unaffected.

findings.defect: Home kept the sample's project count on an empty workspace.
findings.scenario: --only stats on a fresh server fails: Home shows 8 projects (the sample) while the API has none; the full run passed only because the flow had already created a project.
findings.cause: The count was updated only inside if (ws.projects.length).
findings.fix: Set the count before the if.

findings.defect: Home's holdout card was never compared with the API.
findings.scenario: The card shows holdouts opened exactly once over holdout projects (the sample shows 6 / 6); a wrong API count would pass.
findings.cause: The check compared the other cards only.
findings.fix: Compare both numbers of that card.

findings.defect: The Compute page's load was untracked, so the new wait returned before its data.
findings.scenario: On a runner where the jobs read takes over 2 s, the stats check reads 'loading' and raises 'no number in loading'; the mobile check measures the page before a wide jobs table renders.
findings.cause: Compute's enter only started a poll and returned no promise.
findings.fix: Make Compute's first load awaitable: enter returns the first load's promise.

findings.defect: Adding the browser-test target broke a test that pins the Makefile line turning models off.
findings.scenario: rd-check failed because the line that exports DCLAB_NO_LIVE_MODELS had changed.
findings.cause: The new target was added onto the pinned line.
findings.fix: Restore that line and give browser-test its own export line.

outcome: Done (7848118): Chromium drives Home, the chat, the wizard, a run and the brief, checks the numbers on four pages against the API, all 19 pages at 1280 px for console, uncaught, CSP and failed-load errors, and all 19 at 375 px for sideways scroll; about 90 s, no model; checked on files and on PostgreSQL; CI runs it against the container. It found three product faults (Benchmark's overflow, Home's sample count, Compute's untracked load). Open: not in make check-all; a model-driven chat is not covered; the page-state check counts only what the 13.1 tracker sees.
lessons: Never read a metric by a dictionary's key order: JSONB reorders keys, so a check passing on files fails on PostgreSQL.
A browser test that starts counting errors after the first load misses the bootstrap, where errors are most likely.
Fix a layout fault at the element that causes it; a global CSS rule fixes one page and breaks others.
Run a stats check on an empty workspace too: sample values hide when real data happens to exist.
